newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 25.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Friday:
- The presidential election is expected to take place at the end of October following the decision by President Mary Robinson to resign on September 12.
- The pound has come under renewed speculative attack, moving independently of sterling and other European currencies to fall against all.
- The Revenue Commissioners will act on tax information that has emerged from the Dunnes payments tribunal but will wait until the final report has been published before taking any action.
- A post-mortem was being carried out last night on the body of Brendan O'Donnell, the triple murderer found dead at Dublin's Central Mental Hospital yesterday morning.
- Police have foiled an IRA plan to carry out a multi-million pound robbery which could have damaged the peace process.
- Voters face a presidential election at the end of October following yesterday's announcement by Mary Robinson that she will step down on September 12.
- The Revenue Commissioners are to crack down on "high rollers" living lavish lifestyles that are out of line with their declared income.

- Team Aer Lingus has scored a major psychological and financial boost by recapturing the maintenance contract for Virgin Atlantic aircraft which it lost three years ago during a bitter industrial dispute.

- Triple murderer Brendan O'Donnell was hospitalised after a suicide attempt days before he was found dead in bed yesterday. - The Department of Health last night joined with the Voluntary Health Insurance (VHI) in defending its nine percent hike in subscription costs.
- UK Unionist leader Bob McCartney rounded on the Irish and British governments after a parcel bomb addressed to him was defused by Army experts.
